common_name: Chang's Temple Camellia (Zhangjia Cha, Historic Yunnan Semi-Double Reticulata)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; this old Yunnan cultivar, known locally as Zhangjia Cha, has been used as a breeding parent for other reticulata hybrids including Mouchang and the japonica cross Royalty.

directions: Chang's Temple is a long-cultivated Yunnan reticulata whose large, china-rose semi-double flowers carry up to twenty deeply notched petals arranged loosely around a wide central cluster of golden anthers and pale yellow filaments, with some petals marked irregularly rather than solid in color. The shrub grows vigorously but stays comparatively compact for a reticulata, carrying very large dark green leaves that make the mid-to-late-season flowers look proportionally smaller against the foliage. Beyond its garden value, this cultivar has served as a breeding parent, contributing to the reticulata-flowered Mouchang and to the japonica hybrid Royalty bred in California. Grow in humus-rich, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade with wind protection, watering regularly through the growing season and pruning lightly only right after bloom.
sources: American Camellia Society — ACS Camellia Encyclopedia

common_name: Mudan Cha Camellia (Peony Camellia, Historic Yunnan Dwarf Reticulata)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Mudan Cha (literally 'peony tea/camellia') is a dwarf, round-crowned Yunnan cultivar documented since the early twentieth century and used as a breeding parent for Mouchang and other reticulata hybrids.

directions: Mudan Cha, whose Chinese name translates roughly as peony camellia, produces fully double, globose blooms of light pink that fades paler with age, built from roughly thirty petals in five or six whorls: flat ovate outer petals surrounding inner petals that fold, curve, and sometimes fuse at the base to give the flower its rounded, peony-like shape. Unlike the towering habit of many reticulata cultivars, it grows as a dwarf, well-branched shrub with a tidy rounded crown and deeply veined, strongly serrated leaves, though it tends to set comparatively few flowers each February-to-March bloom period. Long documented in Yunnan camellia culture, it has been valued less for mass garden display than as a breeding parent, contributing to hybrids such as Mouchang. Site it in humus-rich, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade sheltered from drying wind, and limit pruning to light shaping right after flowering to preserve its naturally compact form.
sources: Yü & Feng, 'Yunnan Shan Chahua Tuchi' (1958) as cited in ICR
